title: Beef and Ale Pie
subtitle: Slow-braised beef in rich ale gravy under a shortcrust pastry lid
excerpt: Tender chunks of braising beef slow-cooked with ale, mushrooms, and thyme in a thick, glossy gravy, baked under a golden shortcrust pastry lid. A proper British pub pie.

recipe.sourceNotes: Beef and ale pie is one of the great British comfort dishes, combining two long traditions: braised beef stew and pastry crust baking. The use of real ale as the braising liquid is particularly English, drawing on the centuries-old tradition of cooking with beer in the absence of wine, which was expensive and less reliably available. The ale's bitter notes balance the richness of the beef fat and add depth to the gravy. Dark ales (stout, porter, or brown ale) produce a richer, more intense gravy; pale ales are lighter and less distinctive. The beef must be braised for long enough that it falls apart easily with a fork: undercooked braising beef is tough. The filling should be cooked and cooled before it goes into the pastry case so the pastry does not become soggy.

recipeTools.notes: A large casserole or heavy-based saucepan for the filling.
A deep pie dish, about 25 cm diameter.

content.text: Brown the beef in batches: crowding the pan traps steam and prevents browning. Take time over this; the browned crust on the meat builds the flavour of the entire filling. The filling can be made a day in advance and refrigerated. Cool it completely before adding to the pastry, or the pastry lid will be soggy.
Toss the beef with the flour, salt, and pepper. Heat the oil in a large casserole over high heat. Brown the beef in batches, removing each batch as it colours. Do not crowd the pan.

Reduce to medium. Fry the onion and garlic for 5 minutes until softened. Add the tomato puree and cook for 1 minute. Return the beef. Pour in the ale and stock. Add the Worcestershire sauce, thyme, and bay leaves. Bring to a simmer.
Cook covered on a low simmer for 1 hour 45 minutes. Add the mushrooms for the last 30 minutes. The beef should be very tender. Remove the thyme and bay. Cool completely.

Heat the oven to 200 C / fan 180 C / gas 6. Spoon the cold filling into a 25 cm pie dish. Roll out the pastry to a circle slightly larger than the dish. Lay over the filling, trim, crimp the edges, and cut a small hole in the centre to vent steam. Brush with egg wash. Bake for 35 to 40 minutes until the pastry is deep golden. Rest for 5 minutes before serving.
